episode_title: Own the Customer, Not Just the Channel: Amazon, TikTok and the Omnichannel Exit - Neil Twa

real_qa.q: What is the five by five framework for Amazon FBA product profitability?
real_qa.r: The five by five framework requires five products branded in a category, each selling an average of 25 units a day with a minimum profitability of twelve dollars in profit per unit. This turns into approximately $110,000 a year in profit per product, or about $150,000 expected profit per million when accounting for Prime Day and holidays, referred to as the base case for a product over a 12-month run rate.
real_qa.requete: five by five Amazon FBA profitability framework

real_qa.q: How did Neil Twa discover the Seat Pets product innovation strategy?
real_qa.r: Neil discovered Seat Pets while watching television at 4 a.m. feeding his three-year-old daughter. After seeing the infomercial product, he realized Amazon was not capturing demand effectively for it. He and his partner built their own version with innovations including anime-character designs, stronger seams, better fill, and bigger pockets. They sold 2,000 units organically in the first eight weeks, with customers purchasing their version over the infomercial product at five dollars more per unit.
real_qa.requete: Seat Pets Amazon product Neil Twa anime strategy

real_qa.q: What percentage of Amazon.com third-party sales should inform product selection strategy?
real_qa.r: Sixty percent of all Amazon.com sales come through third parties. Neil advises reviewing your last 90 days of Amazon order history and identifying products you purchased between fifty and two hundred fifty dollars that you could potentially sell yourself, based on this high third-party penetration.
real_qa.requete: 60 percent Amazon third party sales strategy

real_qa.q: What is the difference between innovation and invention in e-commerce product trends?
real_qa.r: Innovation refers to differentiation of existing products rather than invention of entirely new ones. Neil uses the Instant Pot as an example—it was an innovation of grandma's crockpot, making it faster, easier, and safer while becoming a billion-dollar company. Air fryers followed as another innovation in the same evergreen demographic space. These innovations in evergreen product categories have longevity, unlike trends like fidget spinners that flame out quickly.
real_qa.requete: Instant Pot air fryer innovation vs invention ecommerce

real_qa.q: What minimum net profit per unit does Neil Twa require before launching Amazon FBA products?
real_qa.r: Neil and his CFO partner set a precedence requiring a minimum of twelve dollars in net profit per unit after accounting for cost of goods, marketing, PPC budgets, and Amazon fees. Early products earning only seven dollars net per unit were deemed insufficient, as this leaves little profit after taxes and personal compensation, requiring unpractical sales volume.
real_qa.requete: Neil Twa twelve dollar minimum profit per unit Amazon

guest.bio_context: Neil Twa has over 17 years of experience in e-commerce with a strong focus on Amazon FBA. He dropped out of college in the early internet era and spent 10 years at Sprint and IBM working on mobile phones, knowledge management systems, and large language models at IBM Watson in Armonk. After leaving IBM in 2007, he transitioned through management consulting and affiliate marketing before discovering physical products on Amazon, launching his first seven-figure brand around 2013-2014.
